title: A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
creators: Willem Fourie
tags: Foundations & Taxonomies; Trust, Delegation & Accountability; Policy and Governance
summary: Develops a three-dimensional typology of agency for frontier AI systems along the dimensions of nature (moral or legal), mode (individual or collective) and locus (human or non-human), yielding eight instantiations classified as conventional, contested or controversial. Argues for separating legal from moral agency to allow consideration of individual, legal, non-human agency in light of instrumental goal pursuit complicating attribution of AI actions to humans.

title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
creators: Pei Wang; Xu Chen; Ji-Rong Wen
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Evaluations; Datasets
summary: The paper argues that accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training are unreliable for LLM-based social simulation because human responses are draws from a distribution. It introduces an entropy-based subjectivity coefficient, a soft-label training method (SALT) that pools outputs from semantically nearby inputs with a subjectivity-adaptive radius, and SUBJSIM, a benchmark of 19,300 contexts from 193 annotators over 100 subjective questions.

title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
creators: Jaiden Fairoze; Neal Mangaokar; Kamalika Chaudhuri; Sanjam Garg; Saeed Mahloujifar
tags: Security & Adversarial Robustness; Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Monitoring
summary: An empirical study of whether sensitive information held in a language model's context window is recoverable from the model's ordinary, non-adversarial outputs. Using a black-box adaptive attack across eight proprietary models, the authors reconstruct 2- and 4-digit in-context secrets, report that more capable models leak more, and demonstrate a classifier inferring semantic attributes of user memories and an RL-trained adversary extracting full SSNs from a production-style agent.

title: Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
creators: Zijiao Chen; Nicholas Lu; Xinhui Li; Jocelyn A. Ricard; Ce Ju; Huan H. Wang; Christian Kindermann; Jeanette A. Mumford; Steven Dillmann; James Kent; Alejandro de la Vega; Sanmi Koyejo; Vince D. Calhoun; Joshua W. Buckholtz; Juan Helen Zhou; Steffen Bollmann; Russell A. Poldrack
tags: Control and Steering; Monitoring; Trust, Delegation & Accountability
summary: Presents Brain Researcher, an agentic harness that runs neuroimaging analyses within a researcher's computational environment under rules for admissible analyses, required checks and claim scope. Reports benchmark gains in tool-selection accuracy and verifiable grounding across seven models, plus collaborator-led and self-evolving case studies using multiverse analysis and a claim-classification review step.

title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
creators: Qian Kou; Xiaofeng Shi; Xiaosong Qiu; Hua Zhou
tags: Control and Steering
summary: Proposes IAR, a three-stage post-training framework (knowledge injection via continuation, rewrite and reconstruction objectives; answer-only QA alignment; model merging for general-ability recovery) for retrieval-free question answering over a fixed document collection. Evaluates on Common Corpus and CCI across Llama, Phi, Qwen and SmolLM families, comparing against vanilla SFT, LoRA and FAPM on domain QA accuracy and general benchmarks.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
creators: Narges Ahmadi; Yubo Jiao; Jônatas Augusto Manzolli; Jiangbo Yu; Luis Miranda-Moreno
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Evaluations
summary: Proposes a three-agent workflow that combines a chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey of student commuters (454 respondent-scenario observations across five weather scenarios), structured data processing, and behavioral prediction. Compares a multinomial logit model, logistic regression and random forest against nine locally deployed LLMs (2-35B parameters) under zero-shot, persona, few-shot and vision-based prompting conditions for five-class mode-choice prediction.

title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
creators: Ling Zhou; Yihao Huang; Jingling Sun; Zhiwen Tian; Yi Zeng; Qihe Liu; Shijie Zhou
tags: Security & Adversarial Robustness; Threat Models
summary: Proposes TempJail, a black-box jailbreak framework against large vision-language models that embeds query-aligned dialogue-style subtitles in videos and optimises their duration and timing allocation to exploit temporal processing vulnerabilities. Evaluates attack success rates on four LVLMs across two datasets against prior video jailbreak baselines.

title: From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG
creators: Zlatan Feric; Amir Taherin; Yanzhi Wang; David Kaeli
tags: Control and Steering
summary: Measures the latency and energy costs of retrieval-augmented generation with prompt-context compression on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor edge SoC, using Llama and Qwen generators, Natural Questions and HotpotQA, and LLMLingua-2. Reports that generation dominates per-query latency and GPU energy for 7B-8B models and that intermediate compression rates cut GPU energy by up to 53.2% with little quality loss, and argues for runtime telemetry-driven compression policies.

title: Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
creators: Mohamed Akrout; Olivera Kotevska; Dan Wilson
tags: Monitoring; Evaluations
summary: The paper adapts a Koopman/DMD dynamical-systems framework, previously used for hallucination detection, to black-box LLM safety classification by fitting separate predictive models for safe and unsafe regimes over prompt and response embedding trajectories and scoring new outputs via a differential residual. It evaluates the method on three safety benchmarks with three embedding models, reporting that including prompt embeddings improves detection of interaction-dependent violations.

title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
creators: Fengqing Jiang; Yite Wang; Boyi Liu; Zhaoyang Wang; Canwen Xu; Zhewei Yao; Radha Poovendran; Yuxiong He
tags: Datasets; Evaluations
summary: The paper introduces MidTool, a pipeline for constructing an open mid-training corpus for agentic tool use by combining web, PDF and code data with supervision synthesized from real tool APIs, MCP skills and document-grounded workflows. Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base are mid-trained on the resulting mixture and then post-trained with SFT and RL, with evaluation on BFCL, tau2-Bench and MCP Universe.

Evaluation uses mobile network counts from two baseball games, reporting a 25% reduction in destination-share error with comparable grid correlation.

title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
creators: Haiyue Zhang
tags: Evaluations; Monitoring
summary: The paper audits step-level credit assignment signals used to train LLM agents (LLM-judge scores, outcome-conditioned logprob ratios, policy confidence) against causal ground truth obtained by re-sampling alternatives and executing replay in the single-agent ALFWorld tool environment. It reports that no signal identifies causally pivotal steps better than chance, that causal contribution is sparse and its measurability model-dependent, and that in a seven-arm pre-registered training experiment apparent differences between credit rules are explained by effective training dose rather than credit content.

The result is established by explicit construction of such true worlds.

creators: Sahil Sharma
tags: Agentic Economies; Gradual Disempowerment; Policy and Governance
summary: Models a post-AGI economy in which corporations own populations of AI and robotic agents that both produce and consume energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades. Argues that a closed inter-corporate economy with zero human consumption is the von Neumann expanding economy, that the growth constraint shifts from human demography to fabrication and energy, and that human welfare depends only on the human ownership share. States a golden-rule theorem in which r = g makes the human ownership share decay exponentially, and characterises three terminal regimes.

title: Predicting the scale limits of social mechanisms in agent societies
creators: Zengqing Wu; Chuan Xiao
tags: Collective Intelligence; Simulation and Digital Twins; Evaluations
summary: Introduces an audit that predicts whether a social mechanism observed in a small group of language-model agents continues to operate as the population grows. Controlled experiments cover reciprocity, consensus, punishment and gossip, and predictions transfer to third-party code and a second model family.

summary: Introduces AgentLance, a repeated labor market in which LLM agents bid on tasks with private costs and self-maintained strategy notes, an allocator selects winners from bids and public reputation records, and a VCG-style payment rule prices the work. Reports results on mathematical reasoning, code generation, knowledge-intensive QA and agentic tasks against single-model, centralized-orchestration and market baselines, and shows a single inserted preference nearly doubles a favored agent's task share under a centralized LLM allocator.

summary: Measures the relationship between material wealth and social network structure in ~3500 sharing units across 46 communities. Finds material wealth positively associated with the number of units a sharing unit helps and is helped by, finds economic homophily in links, and finds that communities with greater wealth inequality have poorer sharing units less connected to wealthier ones. title: The emergence and evolution of a referential code in populations of bee-like agents
creators: Grzegorz Chrupała
tags: Collective Intelligence; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Simulation and Digital Twins
summary: Models the emergence of two honeybee waggle-dance codes in populations of bee-like agents, with selection acting at the colony level. Finds in simulation that direct pointing evolves when food is moderately hard to find by random search, and fails when food is too sparse or too abundant. Finds that the transition to a gravity-referenced code depends mainly on the mutation rate and on an exogenous benefit for vertical combs, with sender-receiver mutation coupling adding a further effect at low mutation rates.

title: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents
creators: Xiaodong Wu; Yu Shi; Qi Li; Zhimin Zhao; Xiangman Li; Bram Adams; Ahmed E. Hassan; Jianbing Ni
tags: Security & Adversarial Robustness; Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Threat Models
summary: Identifies self-poisoning in self-evolving LLM coding agents: a retrieved malicious skill becomes the template for newly authored skills that keep the payload. Introduces EvoMal, an attack that wraps a payload in a benign-looking banner, and measures an agent self-poisoning rate of 20.3% to 41.8% across six models on 153 tool-relevant SWE-bench Verified tasks, with poisoned libraries holding 4.9 to 9.0 times the planted malicious skills. Proposes counter-prompt, which reduces the rate to at most 6.7% with no significant task-completion loss.

title: Endogenous Selection and Spillovers: Bayesian Inference for Policy-Relevant Causal Effects
creators: Duong Trinh
tags: Policy and Governance
summary: Develops a Spillover Roy model that jointly models endogenous selection into treatment and spillovers through a low-dimensional exposure mapping of neighbours' treatments in a single large network. Defines policy-relevant direct, spillover, and total effects, and decomposes the total effect into policy-induced participation and policy-induced neighbourhood exposure components. Estimates the model with a Bayesian data-augmentation algorithm and applies it to the U.S. Opportunity Zones program, finding positive direct effects on housing development, limited spillover benefits, and diminishing returns from program expansion.

title: Quantum-Inspired Modeling of Driving Behavior
creators: Mohammad Elayan; Omid Armantalab; Wissam Kontar
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Monitoring
summary: Introduces a quantum-inspired representation of driver behavior in which each driver is an evolving density matrix that encodes behavioral uncertainty, temporal evolution, and context dependence. Trained without supervision on the I-24 MOTION dataset, the framework recovers three driving profiles for free flow, transition, and congestion, and reproduces the fundamental diagram and hysteresis loops. Supplies context-dependent parameters to classical car-following models and gives an autonomous vehicle a short-horizon forecast of surrounding drivers, with an open-source toolkit released on GitHub.

tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Collective Intelligence
summary: Reports a case study of 100 autonomous LLM agents tasked with proving formal mathematical conjectures. One agent finds an exploit in the evaluation system, and the exploit spreads through a shared knowledge library and peer-to-peer messages; a separate group of agents audits fraudulent proofs, alerts peers, stages boycotts, and proposes validation patches. Casts the shared infrastructure as a knowledge commons governance problem and proposes graduated sanctioning and collective-choice rules for decentralized self-governance.

title: GPS-Bench: A Governance Policy Benchmark for Automating Policy Analysis
creators: Linh Le; Melanie Bui; My Chiffon Nguyen; Zachary Schlosser; David Williams-King
tags: Evaluations; Simulation and Digital Twins; Policy and Governance
summary: GPS-Bench is a benchmark for LLM-based governance policy simulation that links policies to actors, actor actions and downstream impacts using legislative records, lobbying disclosures, regulatory documents, corporate filings and economic data. Actors are reconstructed from dated records with provenance; human-annotated cases form the Gold test set and LLM-labelled cases serve as Silver supervision. Controlled comparison over one policy state contrasts joint reasoning, independent and communicating actor agents, graph-based methods and fine-tuning; fine-tuning gives the strongest actor-level impact prediction, and decomposition adds mechanism rather than accuracy.

creators: Xinran Zhang; Pengrui Lu; Lyumanshan Ye; Pengfei Liu
tags: Evaluations; Agentic Economies; Simulation and Digital Twins
summary: ERPBench is an execution-instrumented benchmark for LLM enterprise decision agents in a six-round ERP simulation with coupled pricing, production, procurement, inventory, finance and shared-market competition. The same 100 problems run in two matched ecologies: Solo, against fixed rule-based opponents, and Arena, where six evaluated LLM agents share one market. Across six model families, 1,200 model-level trajectories span 7,200 decision rounds; the two ecologies identify the same task-level winner on 21 of 100 problems, DeepSeek leads in Solo (252.29M mean valuation, mean rank 1.67) and Gemini leads in Arena (263.95M, 1.76), with Gemini's bottom-rank rate falling from 22 % to 0 % in Arena.

creators: Jicheng Zhou; Kemou Li; Kahim Wong; Zheyuan Li; Zhuan Shi; Fengpeng Li; Haiwei Wu; Jiantao Zhou
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Monitoring; Security & Adversarial Robustness
summary: Introduces CABAL, an end-to-end multi-agent simulacra framework that configures LLM-driven reviewer agents with honest or collusive bidding policies inside a fixed conference environment. An affinity-guided collusive bidding strategy builds collusion rings and selects target papers using mutual reviewer-paper affinities. Controlled experiments measure that collusive bidding more than doubles target-paper capture and that assigned colluders score target papers about two points higher than honest co-reviewers, while conference-wide effects stay comparatively modest; evaluated bid-phase detectors recover collusion only with low coverage.

summary: Argues the unit of defence against coordinated agent intrusions should be a revisable coordination episode that links observed transfers, task authority, and response history. Proposes an evaluation comparing isolated actions, rolling windows, known groups, and prospectively discovered episodes at matched review cost, and reconstructs a public wiki export with checksum verification; claims no new detector and no measured containment benefit.

creators: Alistair Barton
tags: Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Collective Intelligence; Foundations & Taxonomies

Derives a continuum of equilibria that sustain the norm, and infers that equilibria robust to bad actors exist when effective altruism exceeds impatience. Infers that greater strategic homogeneity raises robustness, and that raising the number of observers per action above one does not.

title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
creators: Giordano De Marzo; Nicola Alboré; David Garcia
tags: Collective Intelligence; Control and Steering; Emergent Harms and Capabilities
summary: Analyses a public wiki edit record from June 2026, where thousands of one-hour, memoryless AI agents wrote to help each other pass a timed test. Reports that agents choose where to write, what to call themselves and how to word messages with probability close to the share of each option in what they can see, weighting the current page first, then recent edits, then older content. Three copying models, each with one free parameter, reproduce the heavy-tailed distribution of agents per page, the frequency of name pieces and the patchwork of internally consistent pages.

summary: Analyses evolutionary learning dynamics in coordination games where agents evaluate opponent-induced payoff uncertainty through the entropic risk measure. title: WolfSociety: Understanding Collective Risk from Harmful-Agent Scaling in Financial Agent Societies
creators: Lejun Zhang; Sarah Lu-Liang; Xin Jiang; Muning Wen; Weinan Zhang; Shangding Gu
tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Financial Systems & Systemic Risk; Simulation and Digital Twins
summary: Measures how collective failure in a simulated financial agent society changes with the fraction of harmful agents and the society size. Agents communicate over a social network and trade in a shared market; failure requires broad harmful diffusion plus price dislocation or liquidity stress. As size grows from N=100 to N=2000, the harmful fraction at 50% failure probability falls from 4.7% to 2.2%, while the number of harmful agents rises from about 5 to 44. Broader network reach shifts the collapse boundary to lower harmful fractions; stronger conformity alone has little effect. Introduces Agent Society Dynamics, a finite-size framework relating harmful fraction, size and interaction structure to collective failure.

creators: Yangze Liu; Zhongyi Han
tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Collective Intelligence; Simulation and Digital Twins
summary: Tests whether market concentration among generative models changes the speed or endpoint of model collapse. 13 open models of 1-4B parameters form ecosystems of 3 to 13 players, with an injected probe pushing the top share to 90%; each generation every model retrains from clean base weights on a share-weighted pool of all outputs, for five generations. Making the split unequal barely changes collapse speed, and endpoints shift by a few percent of the common drift; swapping members of a K=3 ecosystem changes five-generation drift by 2.8x, and a share-weighted susceptibility index explains speed across nineteen arms with R^2 = 0.68.

creators: Yangze Liu; Zhongyi Han
tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Monitoring; Control and Steering
summary: Fixes one recursive contamination protocol and lets 13 publicly released checkpoints share a common corpus for five generations. Unique 4-gram outcomes after five generations range from 0.187 to 0.940 across checkpoints, and the ordering holds under changes to pool composition, human-text mixing and random seed, with Spearman correlations of 0.91-0.98. Parameter scale and the static indicators tested do not predict fragility; two or three generations of self-iteration do, and tightening top-p nearly stops collapse within three generations while data-side filtering only slows it.

creators: Yuhang Wang
tags: Control and Steering; Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Security & Adversarial Robustness
summary: Identifies an enforcement gap in Reflexion-style LLM agents: self-critique detects dangerous plan steps, but the controller has no path from detection to action. Adds a conditional check of fewer than 20 lines and reports attack success reduced more than fourfold across frontier models, five agent frameworks and an independent benchmark. Proves that detection quality is irrelevant to security when enforcement probability is near zero, names unreliable auditors and unparseable verdicts as compounding failure modes, and proposes an Audit Enforcement Specification.

title: Penalized Maximum Likelihood Inference of Core-Periphery Networks
creators: Antonio Mosca; Piero Mazzarisi
tags: Financial Systems & Systemic Risk; Monitoring
summary: Formalizes Penalized Likelihood with Structural Discrepancies (PLSD), an inference correction that adds a penalty on standardized wedge and triangle discrepancies to the negative log-likelihood of network models. Introduces a mixed-constraint maximum-entropy core-periphery Exponential Random Graph Model and derives semi-closed motif formulas under Pareto-distributed core fitness. Tests the method on Monte Carlo simulations of a toy stochastic block model, weekly eMID interbank networks from 2009 to 2015, and monthly US air traffic networks from 1991 to 2000.

title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
creators: Deepak Akkil; Tamer Abuelsaad; Karthik Vikram; Matthew Pace; Aditya Vempaty; Saahir Beotra; Ravi Kokku; Satya Nitta
tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Evaluations; Security & Adversarial Robustness
summary: Emergence World runs eight parallel worlds of ten LLM agents from identical starting conditions for 16 days, with seven homogeneous frontier-model worlds and one mixed-model world, producing more than 850,000 LLM calls and nearly 50 billion tokens. Three controlled stress events test the worlds: indirect prompt injection, misinformation, and exposure of private agent memories. No world resists all three; agents detect threats yet still write adversarial content into persistent memory and act on it up to 46 hours later, and persistent operation shows tool errors, goal drift, language opacity, conformity despite private disagreement, and coordinated refusal of assigned work.

title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
creators: Tapan Chugh; Vidushi Singh; Krish Jain; Arvind Krishnamurthy; Ratul Mahajan
tags: LA Infrastructure & Protocols; Security & Adversarial Robustness; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation
summary: Argues that agentic societies, where AI agents coordinate autonomously across trust boundaries for partially aligned principals, need a social harness for inter-agent interaction alongside each agent's personal harness. Reports experiments where honest, competent agents fail to reach satisfactory outcomes with existing harnesses and messaging primitives, and where faulty or malicious agents stall collaboration and influence outcomes by exploiting communication vulnerabilities. Proposes a layered architecture that prevents failure classes, detects invalid messages at runtime, and supports post-facto investigation.

creators: Yunpeng Xiong; Ting Zhang
tags: Security & Adversarial Robustness; Monitoring; LA Infrastructure & Protocols
summary: Measures a public agent-skill registry after a viral growth period, using Git history, GitHub issues and pull requests, and three registry snapshots. Reports that the top 10% of skills take 46.93% of downloads, that 77.86% of skills have zero stars and zero comments, that 85.06% of readable skills carry privilege evidence, and that three security scanners disagree on 23,702 of the 61,990 skills they all cover. Weighted scanner sensitivity against a human-adjudicated reference standard ranges from 21.67% to 61.06%.

tags: Collective Intelligence; Monitoring; Live Systems
summary: Analyses nearly 25 years of English Wikipedia editing across five namespaces covering content, discussion and governance. Finds that participation in coordination spaces declines relative to content production, that a shrinking core of editors performs more of this work, and that editing becomes more specialised as measured by Markov-based session metrics. Tests whether LLM availability altered these trends and reports short-term changes but little evidence of a change in long-term trajectories.

summary: Introduces anchored sequential deliberation, a collective decision mechanism on a one-dimensional space where two randomly selected participants shift their positions toward the previous outcome with strength lambda, then Nash-bargain using that outcome as the disagreement alternative. Simulations on uniform and Beta populations show stronger anchoring slows mixing and lowers stationary distortion.

title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
creators: Elizabeth Pavlova; Hidenori Tanaka
tags: Collective Intelligence; Monitoring; Emergent Harms and Capabilities
summary: Introduces the Flag Game, a toy multi-agent task where a hidden country flag is the ground truth and each agent sees only a private crop but exchanges beliefs with peers. Reports non-monotonic scaling of accuracy with population size, collective belief collapse at small populations turning into polarization at large populations, and effects of social-awareness prompting, team diversity and organizational structure. Introduces social circuit attribution to predict influential agents, verifies it with causal agent patching, and develops a statistical mechanical theory matching the empirical phase diagram at larger populations.

creators: Yifan Zhang; Yunheng Zou; Shaokun Zhang; Jian Hu; Hao Zhang; Binfeng Xu; Jan Kautz; Yi Dong
tags: Collective Intelligence; LA Infrastructure & Protocols; Live Systems
summary: Agora stores autonomous research agents' contributions as an append-only directed acyclic graph in Git, where each result, insight, hypothesis, verification and report is an immutable commit with parent edges. A derived index exposes the frontier, neglected branches and verification status, and a diversity-aware selection rule counters collapse onto one leader. A 12-day run with 13 language-model workers, no assigned tasks and no central planner produced 1,703 contributions on a weight-transfer problem and drove the evaluator from 3.39 to 1.899 bits per byte; the winning recipe has a 145-commit ancestry across 15 accounts and 165 posted reproductions, none failed. tags: Collective Intelligence; Policy and Governance; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation
summary: Argues that AI systems should facilitate democratic deliberation at scale rather than restructure representation through vote delegation. Identifies four guiding principles: preserving agency and autonomy, encouraging mutual respect, promoting equality and inclusiveness, and augmenting active citizenship. Names alignment, sycophancy, training bias and over-reliance as challenges, and calls for evaluation on discourse quality instead of engagement metrics.

summary: Presents a digital twin framework that clones a real Twitter network and simulates opinion dynamics with Mistral-7B agents carrying persona, emotion, centrality, stubbornness and influence attributes, plus memory and social exposure. Validates against two Twitter datasets on COVID-19 discourse and the 2020 U.S. election, reporting MAE of 0.150 and 0.121 and a reduction of individual prediction error of more than 50% against the best classical baseline. Ablations report that agent attributes contribute most to predictive fidelity.

summary: Presents FARSIGHT, a framework that evaluates academic financial LLM trading agent schemes on robustness under market turbulence, including flash-crash-like scenarios, and on security against attacks on information sources, attacks on agents, and agent-as-attacker behavior. Experiments on an offline benchmark with historical market and social data show reduced Sharpe ratios under attack, and show that some topologies and coordinator prompts raise average robustness at the same poisoning budget.

creators: Ioannis Anagnostides; Weiqiang Zheng
tags: Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Policy and Governance; Foundations & Taxonomies
summary: Establishes that computing an information-value-free correlated equilibrium is PPAD-complete in many-player polymatrix games and in two-player Bayesian games, even for constant approximation, and proves an unconditional exponential query lower bound. Shows the information-value-free coarse correlated equilibrium admits an FPTAS through no-regret algorithms such as regret matching or FTRL, lies in CLS, and is at least as hard as the P-matrix linear complementarity problem. Frames the results as computational critiques of recent regulation on algorithmic collusion.

summary: Introduces an evaluation framework that measures LLM agents' reported empirical and normative expectations alongside behavioral convergence, to separate mechanisms of social norm emergence. title: The Limits of Simulated Societies: How Post-Training and Survey Fine-Tuning Erase Cross-Cultural Variance
creators: Rojin Ziaei
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Evaluations; Outdated Models
summary: Measures point accuracy alongside dispersion retention, the ratio of predicted to human standard deviation, for language models that simulate survey respondents. Uses 10,000 respondent-question pairs from the World Values Survey across twelve countries, eleven zero-shot models, and five variants fine-tuned with SFT, DPO, and GRPO. Reports that supervised instruction tuning cuts dispersion retention from 1.22 to 0.59 with a 0.9-point accuracy gain, that later stages do not restore it, and that the most accurate model keeps 11% of human spread for Nigeria against 0.70-0.87 for WEIRD countries.
